summary: Geo cutover: variant affinity mismatch causes split request routing for dedicated tenant
description: Issue summary: During a scheduled geo cutover for a dedicated customer (Peregrine HealthTech) we observed a subset of requests from the tenant being routed to a legacy variant despite an explicit model version pin. Impact: ~12% of requests for the tenant in us-west were answered by redwood-chat-v2.1-legacy (legacy weights) resulting in higher latency and tokenization mismatch with customer post-processing, causing errors in their pipeline. Environment: Production dedicated cluster (us-west) on committed capacity. Canary weight adjustment and region handoff occurred as part of a planned cutover at 2026-03-10T03:00Z. Observed behavior: After the cutover we see session-level split routing: some streams maintain the pinned variant while others are diverted to an older variant. Expected behavior: Tenant-level explicit pin should ensure steady routing to pinned model across the cutover window. This ticket captures investigation, intermediate findings, and proposed mitigations.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer created an explicit model pin for tenant T-234 to redwood-chat-v2.1.
2) Scheduled geo cutover (us-west primary -> us-east warm) with canary weight ramp described in runbook.
3) Triggered cutover at 2026-03-10T03:00Z.
4) Observe that ~12% of requests post-cutover return responses generated by redwood-chat-v2.1-legacy while rest use pinned variant.
5) Attempts to repro with replayed traffic from tracing show same split when requests arrive through the edge pool that drained last.

investigation_notes: Timeline: 03:00 cutover start. 03:02 first split observed in edge logs. Hypothesis A: edge-proxy drain/reshard left behind sessions tied to older routing snapshot, causing stale affinity to prev variant. Hypothesis B: commit for explicit pin was applied to control-plane snapshot after some edge nodes adopted the new routing epoch, leading to inconsistent snapshot visibility. Evidence: session-handoff warnings show stale-session-pin=true on az3 nodes. Control-plane snapshots at 03:01 and 03:03 indicate pin present in later snapshot only. We replayed traffic through a warmed & drained edge pool and observed deterministic split correlated with node epoch. Additional logs point to KV cache population differences between v2.1 and v2.1-legacy which can allow selection logic on edge to fall back when a prefix is missing. Related PRs include an edge-agent change to snapshot refresh timing (PR 411). Initial impact mitigation: increased canary stabilization delay in runbook and triggered an on-demand pin-refresh broadcast to all edge instances. Ongoing: SRE to validate snapshot propagation guarantees and add quorum commit before canary weight shift. Control-plane team investigating commit-ordering and snapshot TTL handling.
comments: Support (Ava Chen) [2026-03-10T04:12Z]: Customer reports ~12% of requests failing post-cutover. Collected logs and traces attached. Escalating to SRE.

SRE (Diego Martinez) [2026-03-10T04:35Z]: Initial triage suggests epoch visibility lag. I pushed an immediate pin-refresh broadcast (control-plane API) to all edge nodes; customer reports a drop in legacy responses to <1%.

Customer (Peregrine Eng - Ravi Patel) [2026-03-10T05:00Z]: After pin-refresh the downstream pipeline still saw occasional schema mismatches, but the error rate dropped. We need assurance this won't recur on future cutovers.

Control-plane (Maya Singh) [2026-03-11T09:20Z]: We're reproducing locally with staged snapshot latency. Adding a commit quorum check to ensure explicit pins land before weight adjustments. Will open PR for coordinated commit barrier.
SRE (Diego Martinez) [2026-03-12T11:05Z]: Rolled temporary control-plane patch to hold canary weight changes until pin commit is observed by >=90% of edge nodes. Monitoring for regressions.
resolution: Workaround applied: broadcasted pin-refresh and temporarily blocked canary weight ramp until pin commit quorum reached; customer errors reduced to acceptable levels. Root cause: race between control-plane pin commit and canary weight change combined with edge snapshot refresh timing that allowed some edge nodes to evaluate routing using an older snapshot. Permanent fix in progress: (1) control-plane will require commit-ack quorum before allowing canary weight adjustments (PR tracked in orchestrator#2087), (2) edge-agent will be updated to perform topology-aware snapshot pulls during cutovers to avoid stale session affinity, (3) add test coverage in cutover e2e tests for explicit-pin + geo handoff scenarios. Follow-ups: schedule postmortem with Runbook/Release owners, update geo-cutover playbook with explicit pin verification step, and run a dedicated chaos test for snapshot-loss scenarios. Targeted rollout of fixes in next release window (2026-03-26).
